title: Fixed-degree pseudo-coherence under restriction through a pseudo-coherent algebra
statement: Let $f:S\to T$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings such that $T[0]$, with its $S$-module structure through $f$, is pseudo-coherent [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex]. For every $m\in\mathbf Z$ and $K\in D(T)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $$K\text{ is }m\text{-pseudo-coherent over }T\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad f_*K\text{ is }m\text{-pseudo-coherent over }S$$ [def-pc-ring-m-pseudo-coherent]. Here $f_*$ is restriction of scalars, induced termwise on representing complexes by keeping the additive groups and differentials and setting $s\cdot k=f(s)k$. This exact functor preserves quasi-isomorphisms. No flatness, surjectivity, Noetherian, or cohomological boundedness assumption is imposed.

source.place: Tag 064Z, lemma-finite-push-pseudo-coherent, equivalence (1) and (2) for a fixed integer m.

proof.text: Restriction keeps the additive groups, differentials, kernels and images, so $H^i(f_*L)=f_*H^i(L)$ for every complex $L$. Thus it preserves and reflects cohomology vanishing and preserves quasi-isomorphisms, giving a functor on the localizations $D(T)\to D(S)$. It commutes with shifts and with the cone formula $C(u)^i=L^i\oplus E^{i+1}$, $d(x,y)=(d_Lx+u(y),-d_Ey)$. Since distinguished triangles are isomorphic to images of cone triangles, it preserves them. Fix a bounded-above finite free $S$-complex $P^\bullet$ modeling $f_*T[0]$. For every finite $r\geq0$, $(P^\bullet)^{\oplus r}$ models $f_*T^{\oplus r}[0]$: kernels and images of its differential are the corresponding finite direct sums, so its cohomology is the direct sum of the cohomology of $P$. It is bounded above and finite free termwise. Hence every finite free $T$-module is pseudo-coherent after restriction, including rank zero.

source.place: Tag 064Z, lemma-finite-push-pseudo-coherent, scalar-restriction identifications and the terms of the finite free approximation; definitions in Tag 064Q.

proof.text: Consequently, for any bounded finite free $T$-complex $E^\bullet$, every term of $f_*E^\bullet$ is pseudo-coherent as an $S$-module by Step 1. The complex is bounded above. Apply [lem-sfb-pseudocoherent-terms-bounded-above] over $S$ to obtain pseudo-coherence of $f_*E^\bullet$. By [lem-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-iff-all-m] it is $q$-pseudo-coherent over $S$ for every integer $q$. Over $T$, the identity of $E^\bullet$ itself witnesses $q$-pseudo-coherence for every $q$.

source.place: Tag 064Z, proof of (1) implies (2), using Tag 064Y, lemma-complex-pseudo-coherent-modules, and Tag 064U, lemma-pseudo-coherent.

proof.text: Suppose $K$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent over $T$. Choose its witness $\alpha:E^\bullet\to K$ and complete it to a distinguished triangle $E^\bullet\to K\to C\to E^\bullet[1]$. In the long exact sequence, for every $i\geq m$, $H^i(\alpha)$ is surjective and $H^{i+1}(\alpha)$ is injective. Exactness gives $H^i(C)=0$ for $i\geq m$. Step 1 gives the restricted distinguished triangle and the same vanishing for $f_*C$. The map from the zero finite free complex to $f_*C$ is therefore an $m$-pseudo-coherent witness. Step 2 makes $f_*E$ $m$-pseudo-coherent. The middle-vertex clause of [lem-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-distinguished-triangle] over $S$ now makes $f_*K$ $m$-pseudo-coherent.

source.place: Tag 064Z, proof of (1) implies (2); Tag 064W, lemma-recognize-pseudo-coherent (1), here proved by the zero witness; Tag 064R, lemma-cone-pseudo-coherent (2).

proof.text: For the converse, suppose $f_*K$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent. Its bounded finite free witness has an upper degree bound $d$; the isomorphisms above $m$ imply $H^i(f_*K)=0$ for $i>\max(d,m)$. Thus $K$ also has a cohomological upper bound. Prove the following uniform assertion by induction on the natural number $n-m+1$: whenever $n\geq m-1$, $H^i(L)=0$ for $i>n$ and $f_*L$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent, then $L$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent over $T$. The base $n=m-1$ holds because all cohomology in degrees $\geq m$ vanishes, so the zero finite free complex is a witness. An upper bound for $K$ can be enlarged to be at least $m-1$, so this assertion will apply to $K$. No largest nonzero cohomology group is required.

source.place: Tag 064Z, proof of (2) implies (1), induction on the upper cohomological degree; Tag 064W (1), zero-witness base case. Agent-explicit uniform induction including the acyclic complex.

proof.text: Let $n\geq m$ and assume the assertion of Step 4 for upper bound $n-1$. Consider $L$ with the hypotheses for upper bound $n$. The same $m$-pseudo-coherent witness for $f_*L$ is an $n$-pseudo-coherent witness: its cohomology maps are isomorphisms for $i>n$, and at $n$ they are surjective (an isomorphism if $n>m$). Apply [lem-sc-finite-cohomology] with ring $S$ and cutoff $n$, using $H^i(f_*L)=0$ for $i>n$. Choose finite $S$-generators $[z_1],\ldots,[z_r]$ of $H^n(f_*L)$ and cycle representatives $z_j\in L^n$ in a representing $T$-complex. These classes also generate $H^n(L)$ over $T$: an expression $\sum s_j[z_j]$ becomes $\sum f(s_j)[z_j]$. Set $E=T^{\oplus r}[-n]$, concentrated in degree $n$, and define a chain map $u:E\to L$ by sending the basis vectors to $z_j$. The cycle equations give $d_Lu=0$, and $H^n(u)$ is surjective.

source.place: Tag 064Z, proof of (2) implies (1), upper-degree induction; agent refinement using Tag 064S, lemma-finite-cohomology (1), to choose a one-degree finite free top approximation.

proof.text: Form the cone triangle $E\xrightarrow{u}L\to C(u)\to E[1]$. For $i=n$, $H^n(E)\to H^n(L)$ is surjective and $H^{n+1}(E)=0$, so the long exact sequence gives $H^n(C(u))=0$. For $i>n$, both $H^i(L)$ and $H^{i+1}(E)$ vanish, so exactness again gives $H^i(C(u))=0$. Hence $C(u)$ has upper cohomological bound $n-1$. Step 1 carries this cone triangle and its cohomology to the corresponding objects over $S$.

source.place: Tag 064Z, proof of (2) implies (1), cone with lower upper cohomological bound; agent refinement using the cycle map of Step 5.

proof.text: Step 2, applied to the one-degree bounded finite free $T$-complex $E$, says that $f_*E$ is $(m+1)$-pseudo-coherent over $S$. Since $f_*L$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent, the first clause of [lem-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-distinguished-triangle] over $S$ makes $f_*C(u)$ $m$-pseudo-coherent. Step 6 verifies the other hypothesis for the induction assertion at $n-1$, so $C(u)$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent over $T$. Finally $E$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent over $T$ by its identity witness. The middle-vertex clause of the same triangle lemma, now over $T$, makes $L$ $m$-pseudo-coherent. This completes the induction and the converse for $K$.

source.place: Tag 064Z, proof of (2) implies (1), two applications of Tag 064R, lemma-cone-pseudo-coherent, and the induction hypothesis.

proof_origin.place: Tag 064Z, lemma-finite-push-pseudo-coherent: forward implication follows its proof; converse refines its upper-degree induction by finite top-cohomology generators from Tag 064S instead of tensoring a whole approximation.
